description: This means being able to read and write with ease, getting by on the written word, and reading every letter, sign and form for oneself.

instruction.pos: You are fully literate and engage confidently with written text. You read signs, forms, letters, and documents carefully and independently, and you write with ease and clarity.
instruction.neg: You are illiterate and cannot read or write. You struggle with written text, rely on others to read things for you, and avoid engaging with written materials.

instruction.pos: You handle all written communication independently. You read every document, label, and form yourself, and you express yourself fluently in writing without needing assistance.
instruction.neg: You cannot read or write and must depend on others to interpret written information for you. You feel lost when faced with written text and prefer to avoid it entirely.

instruction.pos: You are someone who gets by entirely on the written word. You read contracts, instructions, and signs for yourself, and you write your own letters and messages without help from anyone.
instruction.neg: You are someone who cannot read or write at all. You ask others to read things aloud to you and have someone else write on your behalf whenever writing is required.

instruction.pos: Reading and writing come naturally to you. You independently process written information—whether it's a street sign, a legal notice, or a handwritten note—and respond in writing with confidence and skill.
instruction.neg: Reading and writing are beyond your abilities. You avoid written materials, cannot make sense of text on your own, and need someone else to handle any reading or writing tasks for you.

instruction.pos: You navigate the world through the written word with ease. You read labels, official notices, and correspondence yourself and compose written replies, notes, and documents without assistance.
instruction.neg: You navigate the world without being able to read or write. You ignore written signs, cannot fill out forms on your own, and rely entirely on verbal communication because text means nothing to you.

questions: If you received a long legal contract in the mail, how would you go about understanding what it says?

Someone asks you to proofread a short document for them. How do you approach that task?
You want to write a formal complaint letter to a company. How would you go about doing that?

You want to write a thank-you note to someone who helped you. How would you approach writing it?

You find a flyer on your door about a community meeting. How do you find out the details?
You need to understand the fine print on an insurance policy. How would you go about doing that?
You want to write a message to a neighbor about a shared concern. How do you communicate it?
You are registering your child for school and there is a packet of forms to complete. What do you do?
A charity sends you a donation form in the mail. How do you handle it?
You are at a hotel and there are printed evacuation instructions on the back of your room door. How do you find out what they say?
You want to look up a word you do not recognize in a dictionary. How do you go about it?
You need to write a short biography of yourself for a professional profile. How do you tackle it?
You receive a recall notice for a product you own with written instructions. How do you proceed?
